extracted.intended_audience: TCOLE staff, Texas law enforcement agencies, interested persons petitioning for rule changes, and members of the public participating in the rulemaking process
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step procedural guideline for creating, amending, or repealing administrative rules at the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement, including petition content requirements, review and posting procedures, public comment handling, and adoption/effective-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of need to create/amend/repeal a rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff identify a need to create, amend, or repeal a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initiating step in the process; alternatively, an interested person may petition the Commission to request adoption of a rule (see petition requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements under the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may petition the Commission to request the adoption of a rule. The petition shall comply with the requirements of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), Texas Government Code, Chapter 2001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition shall be submitted in writing, and contain a reasoned justification for the rule being proposed, the text of the rule, a concise statement of the statutory or other provisions under which the rule is being proposed, and how these provisions authorize or require the proposed rule. (See 37 Tex. Admin. Code § 211.11.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive director response timeline for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive director shall, within 60 days of submission, either place the petition on the agenda for the next regular meeting or deny the petition in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A denial will be reported at the next meeting. Commission staff or its attorneys may modify the language or format of the petition before it is submitted as a proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff drafting and legal authority review
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff draft a proposed rule. Legal counsel will review the proposal to determine whether it is within the Commission's legal authority to adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal review is required before proceeding to public notice and ensures the proposal is authorized by statute or other law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Meetings Act: agenda posting to Texas Register before meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Open Meetings Act, the proposed rule will be included on a Commission Meeting agenda posted to the Texas Register at least seven days prior to the scheduled Commission Meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven-day posting requirement applies to agenda inclusion so the Commission can lawfully consider the proposed rule at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and discussion at Commission Meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is presented and discussed at the Commission Meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an opportunity for Commissioners and staff to consider the proposal before action to post for notice and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' formal action to approve posting for notice and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to any revisions, the Commissioners take formal action to approve the proposed rule for posting to the Texas Register for notice and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioners are unable to approve the proposed rule, it will be reviewed, rewritten, and re-submitted at a subsequent Commission Meeting or it is abandoned (back to drafting/step 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Texas Register and Commission website posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Following approval of the proposed rule, it is submitted to the Texas Register for posting and posted to the Commission's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability via the Texas Register and the Commission website enables the formal notice-and-comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission receives public comments for 30 days following posting in the Texas Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted during this 30-day period must be considered in determining whether revisions are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to public comments: non-substantive revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the public comments, no revisions or non-substantive revisions are made to the proposed rule as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only non-substantive changes are required, staff can make those adjustments and proceed toward final consideration and adoption without re-running the full proposal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to public comments: substantive revisions require resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the public comments, substantive revisions are made to the proposed rule and the proposed rule is reviewed, rewritten, and re-submitted at a subsequent Commission Meeting or it is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive changes send the proposal back to drafting/review (back to step 2) and typically require re-approval for posting and another notice period as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Open Meetings Act posting before final Commission consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Open Meetings Act, the proposed rule will be included on a Commission Meeting agenda posted to the Texas Register at least seven days prior to the scheduled Commission Meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting applies to the meeting where the proposal (after comments/revisions) will be considered for final adoption; it mirrors the initial meeting-posting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of public comments and addressing them at the meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is presented and discussed at the Commission Meeting. Public comments to the proposed rule are presented and addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners should consider the substance of comments when deciding whether to adopt, modify, or send the rule back for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final adoption action by Commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: If no revisions or non-substantive revisions are necessary, the Commissioners take formal action to adopt the proposed rule and to approve the adopted rule for posting to the Texas Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioners are unable to adopt the proposed rule or if substantive revisions are necessary, the proposed rule will be reviewed, rewritten, and re-submitted at a subsequent Commission Meeting or it is abandoned (back to drafting/step 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and publication of adopted rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Following adoption of the proposed rule, it is submitted to the Texas Register for posting and posted to the Commission's website. The adopted rule becomes effective 20 days after the submission to the Texas Register or on the effective date listed in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When effective, the adopted rule will appear in the Texas Administrative Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff/attorney modification of petition language or format
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff or its attorneys may modify the language or format of the petition before it is submitted as a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should expect possible edits for legal/formatting compliance prior to formal proposal submission.
